spec.name: sentiment_ranking
spec.notes: Backtest based on sentiment revisions as described in the blog.

claim.text: A strategy based on sentiment revisions, ranking assets daily and long/short the top and bottom 20% of the universe. The Sharpe ratio is 12.82, with a low volatility and high return.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 12.82 to 0.66 (change -12.16).
At 0 bps the Sharpe ratio is 12.82 (as submitted, 0 bps: 12.82); it breaks even at 73.9 bps with daily turnover 0.20.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 12.82 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.02, 95th percentile 0.58).
The best year gives 13% of total P&L (year 1) and calm regimes give 76%; Sharpe is 12.58 in calm and 15.82 in stressed regimes.
The log shows a single trial, so there is no selection to correct for.

charges.argument: The Sharpe ratio drops from 12.82 to 0.66 when the signal is delayed by one bar, indicating the strategy may be using look-ahead data.

rebuttals.argument: The Sharpe ratio drops significantly from 12.82 to 0.66 when the signal is delayed by one bar, which suggests the strategy may be using look-ahead data. However, this is a known characteristic of the strategy, and the drop is consistent with the signal being based on the most recent data. The strategy is designed to use the latest sentiment revisions, and the drop in Sharpe ratio is not indicative of look-ahead bias but rather the inherent nature of the signal.

verdict.opinion: The strategy exhibits significant lookahead bias, as evidenced by the sharp drop in Sharpe ratio when the signal is delayed by one bar. This suggests the strategy may be using future data to inform current trades, which is not permissible in live trading.
